newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers shorten US debt positions-MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers shorten US debt positions-MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers turned more bearish on U.S. debt markets in the past week, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
"All else equal, there's probably more selling to do," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark slipped to 108.0 percent--the lowest measure in four weeks--in the week ended January 6, compared with 108.2 percent in the prior week.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 31 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," compared with 24 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 27 percent, up from 10 percent in the week ended December 30.
Fourty-two percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, down from 66 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets inched up to 2.21 percent, against 2.20 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 31 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, down from 32 percent the previous week, while 10 percent underweighted it. The remaining 59 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 51 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 11 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants, who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
